question: The aim of the scheme is to support farmers who suffered damage to their crop and livestock production or production equipment, including fixed assets. The support is in the form of direct grants of up to EUR 200 000 per beneficiary.

The absence of effective actions to address the multifaceted damage caused to agriculture, defence and social cohesion by the Evros wildfires needs to be rectified as quickly as possible. It is also important to point out the relentless tax competition from Bulgaria and Türkiye. Around 50 areas in Europe have been designated as free zones within the customs territory of the EU.

Article 21(4) of the Greek VAT Code (Law No 2589/2000) grants a VAT discount to Aegean islands affected by irregular immigration. In view of this, can the Commission answer the following:
1.
What are the estimated amounts of unused/untapped funding for Evros on a national and regional scale?
2.
Can it adopt a more favourable tax scheme for agricultural businesses, even if it is for a limited time, with a view to speeding up local recovery as much as possible?
answer: 1. Cohesion Policy funds from the 2021-2027 programming period can be mobilised to address the needs of the disaster area. Under the regional programme ‘East Macedonia and Thrace‘, EUR 639 million is allocated to investments in the region, out of which, EUR 31 million are earmarked to climate related risks actions.

The region can also benefit from the national programmes Civil Protection and Environment that have allocated around EUR 1 billion of total public funding to climate related risks. Regarding the 2014-2020 programming period, the EUR 457 million allocated to the programme is expected to be fully absorbed.

Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) foresees support under the Greek Rural Development Programme 2014-2022 (1) and the CAP Strategic Plan 2023-2027 (2), with remaining funds of respectively EUR 1.5 billion and EUR 13.2 billion at national level (3).

These funds may be used by Greece, also for the restoration of agricultural and forestry potential following natural disasters, climatic or catastrophic events and for preventive actions. The Commission has also adopted a support measure of EUR 43.3 million for Greece from the agricultural reserve to address the most affected farmers (4). Support for this measure should be paid by 31 May 2024. 2.

Concerning the adoption of a favourable tax scheme for agricultural businesses, the Commission recalls that when Member States decide to grant state aid, it is up to them to design the state aid measures and determine the form of aid. However, they must do so in accordance with applicable EU State aid rules, laid out, in particular, in Articles 107 and 108 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.
A favourable tax scheme for agricultural businesses constitutes state aid and needs to comply with these rules.
